meta.description: Convert Gram (g) to Kilogram (kg) instantly. 1 g = 0.001 kg. Free, accurate, engineering-grade precision.

content.intro: Convert grams (g) to kilograms (kg) instantly. Both measure weight & mass, so the relationship is strictly linear: each gram equals 0.001 kilograms. Use the converter above for any value, or read on for the formula, a quick lookup table, and practical tips.
content.result_section: One gram is equal to **0.001 kilograms**. To go the other way, one kilogram equals **1000 grams**. For everyday use, rounding to 2–4 decimal places is usually enough; for engineering or scientific work, keep the full precision shown by the converter.
content.formula_section:
The conversion is a single multiplication:

> kilograms = grams × 0.001

Worked example — converting 10 grams:

10 × 0.001 = **0.01 kg**.

To invert, divide by 0.001 (or multiply by 1000).
content.use_cases:
- Cooking and recipe conversions when switching between metric and imperial measurements.
- Travel planning where signage and maps use different unit systems.
- DIY and home-improvement projects that mix metric materials with imperial tools.
- Fitness tracking when devices report in one system and goals are set in another.
- Shipping and logistics where weight and dimensions drive cost.
content.tips:
Keep the factor handy: 1 g ≈ 0.001 kg. For rough mental math, round to the nearest sensible digit.

Mind the units. Gram and Kilogram both measure weight & mass; squared or cubic variants need a different factor (factor², factor³).

When precision matters (engineering, lab work, dosing), avoid rounding mid-calculation — convert once at the final step using the full factor.
content.faq:
**Q:** How many kilograms are in 1 gram?
**A:** 0.001 kilograms.

**Q:** What's the formula to convert g to kg?
**A:** kilograms = grams × 0.001.

**Q:** How do I convert kg back to g?
**A:** Multiply by 1000 (or divide by 0.001).

**Q:** Is rounding to 2 decimal places accurate enough?
**A:** For most everyday uses, yes. For scientific or engineering work, use the full precision from the converter.

**Q:** Does this g to kg converter work offline?
**A:** Yes — all math runs in your browser, no network required after the page loads.
